thesis: The three conviction probabilities do not, by themselves, identify whether any judge completely removed the forbidden consideration from deliberation because of the rule. The strongest defensible argument grants comparable baselines and genuine rule-guided discounting, then constructs two populations with identical observable rates but different incidences of complete exclusion. It expressly leaves open successful guidance under a broader, action-based account.
claimed_contribution: A targeted non-identification argument concerning Sekine’s interpretation of one judicial experiment: an explicit mixture model and a universal partial-discounting model reproduce the same rates, and specified extensions remain equivalent across a range of evidence strengths. The manuscript acknowledges that observational-equivalence methods, discounting versus discarding, and decisions versus their motivating bases are inherited.

findings.manuscript_location: What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us — paragraph beginning “In §3”: “Footnote 43 explicitly leaves room for guidance by exclusionary reasons beyond excluding the target reasons”; subsequent discussion of broader guidance.
findings.claim: The discussion has a direct philosophical predecessor that is acknowledged only indirectly through Sekine’s footnote.
findings.analysis: Ehrenberg distinguishes guidance from accidental conformity and explains how exclusionary reasons can guide action contrary to their valence. He also distinguishes deliberative assessment from membership in the reasons motivating action. These arguments directly inform the manuscript’s scope restriction. Sekine’s note 43 explicitly credits him. A direct citation would clarify this intellectual relationship. This is a bibliographic omission, not a false attribution or a refutation. Ehrenberg’s account does not itself establish that residual-weight Model B satisfies successful exclusion. See [Ehrenberg, pp. 72–75](https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/pdf/10.1080/20403313.2023.2297581).
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The numerical result survives. The distinction between successful guidance and a verdict’s direction should be presented as inherited; the manuscript’s application to its particular models remains separate.
findings.repair_conditions: Cite Ehrenberg directly and distinguish his account of motivational exclusion from the manuscript’s deliberately unresolved interpretation of rule-caused partial discounting.

findings.manuscript_location: What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us — “The general method of comparing models with the same observable implications is inherited”; equations “q × 0.491 + (1 − q) × 0.077” and “P(x > kd) = 0.491 − kd.”
findings.claim: There are close methodological parallels beyond the cited literature, although neither inspected parallel establishes this manuscript’s specific result.
findings.analysis: Yoo shows how latent classes interpreted as ignoring attributes can instead approximate unmodelled heterogeneity, including simulations without actual non-attendance; see [§§II–III](https://research.economics.unsw.edu.au/RePEc/papers/2012-47.pdf). Allen proves observational equivalence between full and limited consideration models over bounded utility variation; see [§3, Proposition 1](https://arxiv.org/html/2405.13945v1). These are substantive parallels concerning identification of an unobserved decision process. Their objects differ: consumer attributes or available alternatives, rather than rule-guided removal of an acquired reason. Yoo’s simulations also differ from exact population equivalence. The manuscript already disclaims novelty for the general method, so this is a modest positioning gap.
findings.effect_on_conclusion: The contribution remains an application and explicit construction, not a new general method for distinguishing ignored considerations from weakly weighted ones. No inspected source displaces the specific judicial application.
findings.repair_conditions: Briefly locate the construction beside relevant identification literature and explain the differences in objects, assumptions, and evidential targets. Do not describe the manuscript as a direct corollary without supplying a formal mapping.

surviving_contribution: Under the heading “What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us,” the equations and paired-model table establish a specific inferential limit: 49.1%, 7.7%, and 20% are compatible both with approximately 29.7% complete excluders and with none. The variation argument adds that the specified models agree throughout 0 ≤ d ≤ 0.491 but diverge at d = 0.6. These calculations are internally consistent on inspection. After accounting for the predecessors, the distinct remainder is their application to this experiment and to the precise philosophical achievement being measured. The result concerns compatibility and identification, not the actual prevalence of exclusion, equal model plausibility, or the impossibility of broader guidance. I did not locate this complete application in the primary texts inspected; that is a limited-search conclusion.
remaining_questions: Under “What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us,” “A defender might count this as successfully refraining from an acquittal for the prohibited reason” remains an open interpretive question. What account of guided nonperformance licenses that classification? The manuscript correctly makes its narrow result independent of the answer.

Under “What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us,” “Its description also invites a stronger interpretation” identifies an interpretive choice rather than an explicit definition supplied by Sekine. How much argumentative importance should attach to correcting that stronger reading once the broader defence is conceded?

Under “What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us,” the extension fixes q and k while varying d. Whether any practical manipulation preserves these parameters and the baseline distribution is unanswered. The manuscript explicitly presents this as an illustration, so this is not a demonstrated defect.
Rocchè’s full argument could not be inspected. Its relationship to the manuscript’s narrow empirical correction remains unresolved, despite its direct place in Sekine’s discussion.
limitations: The complete supplied manuscript, including its bibliography, was read. The supplied hash was retained without recomputation.

Four cited works were checked in publisher or institutional full text. For Wistrich, Guthrie and Rachlinski, institutional identity records opened, but their PDF links failed. The relevant original-paper passages were read in a public third-party transcription; they were not checked against a publisher scan. Those citation checks are therefore marked partially_verified.

Rocchè’s institutional record and abstract opened, but the repository PDF returned 403, OpenEdition presented a bot challenge, and ResearchGate supplied no full text. No conclusion about his detailed argument or the absence of a matching construction is warranted.
Search results were used to locate texts, not as substitutes for reading them. Unopened results were not counted as inspected predecessors.
The search covered several formulations and adjacent literatures but was not exhaustive. No claim of comprehensive originality, priority, or absence of further predecessors is made.
Published experimental reporting was checked; underlying participant data were not obtained, and the reported Fisher test was not independently recomputed.
Only public web research was used. No agents, local files, shell tools, project history, private sources, author contact, manuscript modification, or publication actions were used.

closest_predecessors.overlap: Discusses the same rates, their statistical weakness, and discounting rather than discarding evidence.
closest_predecessors.difference: The inspected discussion does not construct exact population-equivalent models with different numbers of complete excluders.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The explicit non-identification construction and its application to Sekine’s stronger empirical inference.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Wittlin pp. 1759–60, note 143; manuscript heading “What the Verdict Does Not Tell Us,” “The further question is whether even perfectly established rates would identify any complete excluder.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: A decision can remain fixed while its basis changes; second-order basing has causal and appraisal requirements.
closest_predecessors.difference: Keeling develops an account of basing, rather than an identification analysis of conviction probabilities.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: Application of the inherited distinction to what verdict observations establish.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Keeling §3.1 and §3.2.4, pp. 806–07 and 811–12; manuscript “The following examples apply that inherited distinction.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Guidance can coexist with acting against an exclusionary reason’s valence; deliberation and motivating reasons must be distinguished.
closest_predecessors.difference: Ehrenberg does not supply the manuscript’s probability models or a defence of universal partial discounting as successful exclusion.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: Showing precisely why those models challenge complete removal without settling every account of guidance.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Ehrenberg pp. 72–75; manuscript “The paired models then cease to contrast success with failure under that conception.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Model-based estimates of ignored attributes can reflect nonzero sensitivities and heterogeneity.
closest_predecessors.difference: The mechanism is econometric approximation and misspecification, not the manuscript’s exact uniform-threshold equivalence or rule-guided achievement.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: An exact, elementary construction tied to a particular philosophical inference.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Yoo §II, equations (1)–(3), and §III’s examples; manuscript “Knowing those probabilities exactly would not choose between the models.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Different latent consideration structures can have identical choice probabilities over a whole bounded range.
closest_predecessors.difference: Allen studies exclusion of alternatives from consideration sets under nonparametric random utility. The manuscript studies the weight of a reason while retaining the verdict alternatives and specifying stable response parameters.
closest_predecessors.remaining_contribution: The application to reason exclusion, including its distinction from broader guided nonperformance.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Allen §3, Proposition 1, and §3.1; manuscript “Throughout 0 ≤ d ≤ 0.491, their conviction probabilities remain identical.”

closest_predecessors.overlap: Investigates information acquisition as well as compliance and considers competing explanations.
closest_predecessors.difference: Avoiding acquisition is distinct from removing an already acquired consideration from a decision’s basis.
closest_predecessors.evidence_location: Hoeft et al. §§3 and 6; manuscript “declining to acquire information and excluding a consideration already acquired are different routes.”
